commands_run: cd spring-boot-admin-server && mvn -B -o -q -DskipTests compile >/dev/null 2>&1; CP="target/classes:$(find /root/.m2/repository -name '*.jar' | tr '\n' ':')"; mkdir -p /tmp/povout && javac -proc:none -cp "$CP" -d /tmp/povout /workspace/repo/.security-pipeline/pov/SpelInjectionPov.java && java -cp "/tmp/povout:$CP" de.codecentric.boot.admin.server.notify.SpelInjectionPov
output_json.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches 3 product files and 3 test files. Product change is identical in all three notifiers: swap `new StandardEvaluationContext(root)` + `addPropertyAccessor(new MapAccessor())` for `SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors(new MapAccessor(), DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess()).withRootObject(root).build()`, with matching import changes. MicrosoftTeamsNotifier additionally widens helper method signatures from StandardEvaluationContext to the EvaluationContext interface (mechanical, required since SimpleEvaluationContext is not a subtype). No vulnerable functionality removed beyond the intended SpEL restriction; legitimate property/ternary/string templating still works. Test changes add one CWE-094 regression test per notifier asserting `#{T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime()}` throws EvaluationException — additive, not a weakening of existing assertions. The POV file (pov.diff) is unchanged/untouched by the patch. No unrelated or broad behavior added.
issues: Non-blocking (out of scope): six other notifiers in the same package (Telegram, OpsGenie, Discord, Pagerduty, Hipchat, DingTalk) use the identical StandardEvaluationContext pattern and share the same CWE-094 class; they were intentionally left unchanged since the alert scoped only the three flagged notifiers. Recommend a follow-up to remediate them the same way.
output_json.pov_result: Reran the exact original pov_command via the Docker wrapper against the patched worktree. Output: "getText threw (payload rejected): SpelEvaluationException: EL1002E: Constructor call: No suitable constructor found on type java.io.File", rendered value null, marker created false, "NOT VULNERABLE: SpEL code injection was blocked." Exit code 1. The attacker-controlled `#{new java.io.File(...).createNewFile()}` payload no longer executes. (Confirmed the same POV exits 0 / creates the marker on unpatched code per the recorded before-patch run.)
output_json.regression_result: Reran `mvn -B -Dtest=SlackNotifierTest,LetsChatNotifierTest,MicrosoftTeamsNotifierTest test` via the Docker wrapper: BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 23, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 (Slack 6, LetsChat 3, MsTeams 14). Pre-existing tests verifying default/custom template rendering still pass, and the new injection-rejection tests pass.
output_json.summary: The patch fixes CWE-094 SpEL code injection in the three flagged notifiers (SlackNotifier, LetsChatNotifier, MicrosoftTeamsNotifier) by replacing the permissive StandardEvaluationContext with a restricted SimpleEvaluationContext (MapAccessor + read-only DataBindingPropertyAccessor), which structurally forbids type references, constructor calls, and arbitrary method invocation. I independently reran the unmodified POV against the patched code: it exited 1 with the payload rejected (SpelEvaluationException, no marker file). Regression tests for all three notifiers passed (23/23). The fix is minimal, targeted, and preserves legitimate property/map templating.
